idiom_name: named class method (Order.from_cart) with private_class_method :new; Data.define for immutable values
implementation_notes: Ruby's new is an ordinary class method, so the factory is realized by defining a domain-named class method and calling private_class_method :new so the named path is the only documented door; immutable value-shaped products use Data.define (Ruby 3.2+), whose instances are frozen on creation and whose member arity is checked by Data#initialize. What replaces the classic factory class is the class method on the aggregate or a small factory object; a separate factory class is justified when creation must reach through repositories, translate an external payload, or build several aggregates in one transaction.
code_sketch:
class Order
  private_class_method :new

  def self.from_cart(customer_id, cart_items)
    raise DomainError, 'cannot open an empty order' if cart_items.empty?

    lines = cart_items.map { |item| Line.from_cart_item(item) }
    new(OrderId.generate, customer_id, lines, :draft)
  end
end
pitfalls: private_class_method :new does not stop allocate, Marshal.load, dup/clone or ORM hydration from producing instances that never passed the factory.
Data instances are frozen only shallowly; freeze nested arrays/hashes on the way in or expose copies, otherwise callers can mutate the aggregate's contents.
ActiveRecord already owns construction (new/find/create!); layering a factory on an ORM model duplicates creation paths unless every caller and association is routed through it.
